walkthroughs.h2: What makes a good exchange surface
walkthroughs.body_html:
Exchange surfaces have a large surface area, are thin and have a good blood supply.

Alveoli have all three: millions of tiny sacs, walls one cell thick, capillary network.

Red blood cells carry O₂. White blood cells fight infection. Platelets clot. Plasma dissolves glucose, hormones, CO₂ and urea.

RBCs are biconcave, have no nucleus, and contain haemoglobin.

Right side pumps deoxygenated blood to lungs. Left side pumps oxygenated blood to body.

Blood reaches body cells at higher pressure — fast O₂ delivery for active animals.
